dominant_strengths: Strong macOS-native chrome with traffic lights, segmented controls, and inspector panel feels authentically Finder-adjacent and trustworthy
Information hierarchy is excellent: pinned/modified/earlier groups, status pills, and collaborator avatars communicate state at a glance
Conflict resolution is surfaced contextually with amber banner, inspector CTA, and conflict badges — meaningful problem framing
dominant_weaknesses: Color system leans on many small accent dots (urgent/approved/client/avatars) creating visual noise that competes with the conflict signal
Inspector preview is a generic gradient placeholder — feels decorative rather than informative for a 128-page Figma file
Row density and column alignment are slightly inconsistent (size column wraps, status pills float) hurting scan rhythm
fix_priorities: Tighten table column grid: right-align sizes, fix status pill column, unify timestamp formatting
Reduce accent-color count or desaturate secondary dots so the amber conflict state remains the singular alert
Replace the abstract inspector thumbnail with an actual page/frame preview to justify the panel's footprint
rationale.norman_balance: Behavioral utility leads with strong stateful affordances, visceral polish is competent but restrained, and reflective payoff is modest since the metaphors stay conventional.
rationale.intent_fit: Yes — it reads as a credible 'improved' file browser by foregrounding collaboration conflicts and inspector context rather than just listing files.
